title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 118
paragraphs: So stand these matters. But of the seven men who had risen against the Magian, it happened that one—Intaphrenes—was put to death immediately after their uprising, for an outrage I shall relate. He wished to enter the king's palace and confer with the king. For the law, in fact, was that those who had risen against the Magian were permitted to enter the king's presence without being announced, unless the king happened to be lying with his wife. Accordingly, Intaphrenes did not think any announcement necessary, but as he was one of the seven, he wished to go in. The gatekeeper and the messenger-bearer, however, tried to prevent him, saying the king was lying with his wife. But Intaphrenes, believing they were not telling the truth, drew his sword, cut off their ears and noses, and stringing these onto his horse's bridle, tied them around their necks and let them go.
